speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
text: asked the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health whether the Ministry will consider a tiered approach to MediSave withdrawal limits as an enhancement to the MediSave 500/700 scheme by taking into account factors such as age and the number of chronic conditions under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP).

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: MediSave is intended to help Singaporeans afford a range of healthcare needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Two dominant ones are: managing chronic long-term diseases and larger, one-off costs associated with hospitalisations, which tend to be incurred later in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Coordinating Minister for Social Policies and Minister for Health)
text: Hence, MediSave withdrawal limits are reviewed regularly to judiciously balance between meeting current healthcare needs whilst preserving their MediSave savings for future healthcare needs.
This will also help defray medical expenses of Singaporeans including those with long-term medical needs and chronic diseases.
We will continue to regularly review the MediSave scheme.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: As we do screening for Healthier SG, we are bound to see increases in chronic diseases in younger adults as well.

speaker: Dr Hamid Razak (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I just want to find out if the Ministry is tracking the burden of this disease by different age groups to better inform us of future changes to the Flexi-MediSave scheme.
